newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani vegoil rates seen rising next week.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani vegoil rates seen rising next week.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil rates are expected to gain next week after a slight increase in international prices, dealers said on Saturday.

"Local vegetable oil rates will post a nominal gain in line to the increased prices abroad," dealer Ziaul Haq said. "The arrival of cottonseed from Punjab province has also slowed down a bit as the cotton season is heading towards its close."
Dealers said vegoil stocks fell to 77,000 tonnes this week from 111,000 tonnes last week.

RBD palm oil and palm olein stocks fell to 70,000 tonnes from 90,000 last week. Soybean oil and sunflower oil stocks fell to 15,000 tonnes from 17,000. The Ghee Corporation of Pakistan (GCP) has 2,000 tonnes of palm oil and palm olein in stock compared to 4,000 last week.
The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) bought 4,500 tonnes of RBD palm oil for the GCP on Thursday at $529.40 per tonne C & F from Pan Century for shipment by December 10.
Dealers said the had TCP scrapped its tender for 2,000 tonnes of RBD palm olein, feeling that the two quoted prices, $571 and $568.70 per tonne, were too high.
One dealer said Pakistan was likely to enter the market again in the next two weeks.

The vessel Wawasan Megah was discharging 9,900 tonnes of palm oil at Karachi Port, while the Jian She-33 with around 6,000 tonnes of palm oil and the Petr Shimbt with 7,500 tonnes of soybean oil were at the outer anchorage.
The Vanino was expected to arrive on November 26 with around 3,600 tonnes soybean of oil and the Helena was due on November 20 with 6,000 tonnes of palm fatty acid distillates.
